conventions.convention: The ridgeless estimator is X⁺y, the minimum-Euclidean-norm least-squares solution, including when exact interpolation is impossible.
Prediction risk averages over training noise and an independent isotropic test feature conditional on the design; it measures error against the noiseless signal and adds no test-label noise variance.

The asymptotic design consists of upper-left blocks of one infinite real iid array with mean zero, variance one and finite fourth moment. Signals are deterministic with fixed norm r ≥ 0; AC is assumed, and γ = 1 is excluded.
Fill distance uses Euclidean distance on a closed positive-side-length cube. The uniform-sampling lemma assumes Countable Choice and normalized Lebesgue measure.
Polynomial reproduction concerns total degree at most n, has coefficient ℓ¹ bound Aⁿ under 2nh_X/L ≤ κ, allows rotated cubes and requires no separation or choice principle.
The Gaussian kernel is exp(−‖x−z‖²/(2σ²)) with σ > 0. Its power function is the RKHS distance of a kernel section from the finite sample-section span; Countable Choice is assumed.
The noiseless sampling estimate holds on one event simultaneously for every RKHS interpolant; its right side retains both the target norm and interpolant norm.
The neural-network and forest curves are reports of specified finite experiments, without a universal double-descent assertion.

load_bearing.statement: For deterministic X and β, independent centered noise with covariance σ²I and independent centered test features with covariance I, conditional prediction risk equals ‖(I−X⁺X)β‖² + σ² tr((XᵀX)⁺) = ‖(I−X⁺X)β‖² + (σ²/n) tr(S⁺), where S=XᵀX/n.

For each integer d ≥ 1 there are A > 1 and κ > 0 such that, for any closed cube of side L > 0 and finite nonempty sample set X, if n ≥ 1 and 2nh_X/L ≤ κ, then every real polynomial of total degree at most n satisfies sup_Ω|p| ≤ Aⁿ max_X|p|. At each x ∈ Ω, real coefficients reproduce all these polynomials simultaneously with sum of absolute values at most Aⁿ. Rotated cubes are allowed; no separation or choice principle is required.

Assuming Countable Choice, for the real Gaussian RKHS on a fixed closed positive-side-length cube there are C,c,h₀ > 0, depending only on d, Ω and σ, such that every finite nonempty X with 0 < h_X ≤ h₀ satisfies sup_Ω P_X ≤ C exp(−c|log h_X|/h_X).

Assuming Countable Choice, independent uniform samples on a product cube of side L have, for every sufficiently large n, probability at least 1−1/n of Euclidean fill distance at most C_d L(log n/n)^(1/d), where C_d=2√d·2^(1/d).

Assuming AC, for upper-left blocks of one infinite real iid mean-zero, variance-one, finite-fourth-moment array with p_n/n → γ ∈ (0,∞) excluding 1, zero-signal conditional prediction risk converges almost surely to σ²γ/(1−γ) for γ < 1 and σ²/(γ−1) for γ > 1, under the stated independent noise and isotropic test-feature assumptions.

Under AC, the stated nested real iid finite-fourth-moment design, deterministic signals of fixed norm r ≥ 0, independent centered noise of covariance σ²I and independent centered test features of covariance I, conditional prediction risk converges almost surely to σ²γ/(1−γ) for 0 < γ < 1 and r²(1−1/γ)+σ²/(γ−1) for γ > 1. No limit is asserted when p_n/n → 1.
Under the isotropic ridgeless risk theorem's hypotheses, B_n=‖(I−X_n⁺X_n)β_n‖² and V_n=(σ²/n)tr(S_n⁺) converge almost surely to 0 and σ²γ/(1−γ) for γ < 1, and to r²(1−1/γ) and σ²/(γ−1) for γ > 1.

published_dependencies.used_for: The four Penrose equations and the meaning of X⁺.
Finite real SVD, including rank-zero cases, and pseudoinverse trace identities.
Existence and uniqueness of the pseudoinverse and identification of its SVD formula.
The equivalent minimum-norm characterization of ridgeless regression.
The precise countable-choice assumption in the measure and RKHS arguments.
The choice assumption carried by the asymptotic spectral suppliers.
Mutual independence and a common law for uniform samples and nested design entries.
Normalized Lebesgue sampling on a cube.
Half-open box volumes in the fill-distance partition.
Measurability and measure preservation when partition cells differ by boundary subsets.
Nullity of cube and partition-cell boundary faces.
Bounding the probability that any partition cell is empty.
Choice-free compactness of cubes and finite-dimensional simplices.
Compactness of the finite symmetric convex hull in polynomial reproduction.
Attainment of polynomial maxima and nearest points in compact convex sets.
Finite trigonometric-polynomial calculations in the polynomial norming proof.
The unit modulus of exp(it).
Differentiating the trigonometric kernels and coordinate substitutions.
Transporting uniform sampling between a rotated cube and a product cube.
The translation component of the cube-coordinate transformation.

seams_checked.note: Checked the cited kernel definition, Gaussian positive-semidefiniteness example, canonical RKHS construction and finite-dimensional projection lemma against their consumer uses. Real scalars, Countable Choice and finite section spans are preserved; invertibility of the Gram matrix is not assumed.

The risk-closure corollary supplies exactly the positive-fixed-signal-norm limits cited by the zero-signal lemma and risk theorem, with the same nested real iid array, finite fourth moment, deterministic signals, AC, noise/test independence and γ ≠ 1. The zero-signal extension is proved locally using signals e₁ and 2e₁ rather than attributed to the supplier.
